title: QUIC: Fix running dissectors on 0-RTT data
description:
Fixes the QUIC dissector not parsing 0-RTT data completely. The contents of the 0-RTT packets needs to be interpreted as the protocol the client sends in its ALPN. Because the wireshark TLS utils only provides a way to get the ALPN decided on by the server in the ServerHello and we are parsing 0-RTT data before the SeverHello, a new method `tls_get_client_alpn` was added for getting the ALPN that the client wanted (The first in the list).

Because the protocol selected by the server might not match what was sent in the 0-RTT data a new field `zrtt_app_handle` was added to `quic_info_data`, and the `quic_packet_info` for the packet being processed was plumbed up to `process_quic_stream` so it can decided what protocol to pass to `call_dissector_with_data`. I'm not sure if there was a more accessible place to access `packet_type` but I couldn't find it in the other arguments.

I wasn't able to find a quick way to test the situation of a client sending 0-RTT data but the server selecting a different protocol so that portion of this code is untested. I have tested that this at least works for HTTP/3 0-RTT data sent by Chrome.

notes.body:
In your experience, is this a fix necessary only live capture / single-pass tshark?

For example: [quic-v2-final-constants.pcapng](/uploads/a89409a1cf910dab5d8ac92044bf37d6/quic-v2-final-constants.pcapng) has HTTP 0-RTT data in the first frame and it works when opened and displayed in Wireshark, or in tshark with -2.

This seems to be necessary in all cases, in the sample you provided the HTTP/3 dissector is only parsing the 0-RTT data after the first pass has already been completed so you only see as far as "Frame Payload" in the dissection of HTTP/3 data in 0-RTT packets. With this patch the HTTP/3 dissector is called during the first pass (or whatever PINFO_FD_VISITED is checking, not sure what to call it) so you see the headers fully parsed and displayed.
Ah yes, I see what you mean.
An example where the server rejects the client's assumptions and the stream has to be reset would be useful too, and probably isn't handled correctly currently.
Yeah, I'm not sure, I will investigate and try to find out what needs to be done.

Ok, since the server rejecting the client's 0-RTT data (whether it be by choosing a different ALPN or any other reason) would make the entire HTTP/3 dissector need to "rewind" everything that has happened including any dissectors after it, I think it's better to simply make a 3rd stream state in `quic_info_data` (besides client_streams/server_streams) and detect in packets after the ServerHello if the 0-RTT data was accepting and if so re-use the stream state that had the 0-RTT data fed in and if not just make a whole new state state. Does that sound correct to you?

Since that is kinda beyond the scope of this patch I will make a new PR for that if you're ok with that.
That generally sounds correct, and I agree, it seems like something that will take a different MR and hopefully a sample capture.
